steps.say: Dilated cardiomyopathy represents the commonest primary myocardial disease in children, manifesting as impaired systolic function and ventricular dilation.
steps.tx: Clinical investigation explores **dilated cardiomyopathy etiology**. DCM is the most common pediatric cardiomyopathy (**50-60%**), caused by genetic mutations (cytoskeletal, sarcomeric), viral myocarditis, inborn errors of metabolism, or anthracyclines, presenting with systolic dysfunction and ventricular dilation. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

steps.say: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy features asymmetric myocardial thickening that frequently produces dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
steps.tx: Molecular biology elucidates **HCM genetic basis**. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is predominantly autosomal dominant and caused by mutations in sarcomeric genes (**MYH7, MYBPC3**, TNNT2) in approximately **60%** of familial cases, featuring asymmetrical septal hypertrophy and myofibrillar disarray. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

vis.caption: Cardiac MRI in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy displaying asymmetrical septal hypertrophy and outflow tract narrowing. Illustration: StewardMD original.
vis.alt: MRI image demonstrating pronounced asymmetric septal hypertrophy.

steps.say: Maternal diabetes exposes the developing fetal heart to hyperinsulinism, inducing transient myocardial hypertrophy that regresses after delivery.
steps.tx: Neonatal screening evaluates **infant of diabetic mother HCM**. Transient asymmetric septal hypertrophy occurs in **10-20%** of infants of diabetic mothers due to fetal hyperinsulinism; it is typically self-limiting and regresses spontaneously within **6-12 months** of age with conservative management. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

left.title: Infant of Diabetic Mother HCM
points: Fetal hyperinsulinism acts as an anabolic growth hormone on cardiac myocytes
Induces disproportionate interventricular septal hypertrophy in 10-20% of infants
Self-limiting physiological phenomenon; completely regresses within 6 to 12 months

right.title: Familial Genetic HCM
points: Autosomal dominant mutations in sarcomeric genes (MYH7, MYBPC3)
Histological hallmark is progressive myofibrillar disarray and interstitial fibrosis
Permanent and progressive pathology carrying lifelong sudden death risk

steps.say: Identifying children with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who are at elevated risk for sudden cardiac death dictates life-saving defibrillator implantation.
steps.tx: Stratifying **HCM sudden death risk factors** guides ICD placement. Pediatric HCM sudden cardiac death risk factors: extreme LV hypertrophy (**septal thickness >= 30 mm** or z-score >= +6), unexplained syncope, non-sustained VT, and family history of SCD warranting implantable defibrillator evaluation. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

rows: Strong independent risk factor for ventricular arrhythmias
Recent episodes not attributable to neurocardiogenic syncope
Signifies transient ventricular tachyarrhythmia or outflow shutoff
Non-sustained VT on ambulatory Holter monitoring
Marker of myocardial electrical instability and scar
Sudden cardiac death in first-degree relative <40 years
Reflects malignant sarcomeric gene mutation phenotype

steps.say: In patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, positive inotropes and vasodilators worsen dynamic obstruction and must be avoided.
steps.tx: Pharmacological precautions mandate **inotropic contraindication in HCM**. Digoxin, positive inotropes, and vasodilators are contraindicated in obstructive HCM because they increase the dynamic left ventricular outflow tract gradient by augmenting contractility and decreasing ventricular end-systolic dimensions. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

left.title: Contraindicated Inotropes (Digoxin, Milrinone)
points: Augments ventricular myocardial contractility and ejection velocity
Shrinks end-systolic cavity volume, narrowing the subaortic outflow tract
Exacerbates systolic anterior motion (SAM) and increases gradient

right.title: Contraindicated Vasodilators (Nitrates, ACEi)
points: Decreases systemic arterial vascular resistance and ventricular afterload
Reduces ventricular end-diastolic chamber filling and preload
Dramatically worsens dynamic subaortic obstruction, provoking syncope

steps.say: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is an uncommon pediatric disorder characterized by severe diastolic dysfunction despite preserved ventricular cavity dimensions.
steps.tx: Prognostication recognizes **restrictive cardiomyopathy prognosis**. RCM is the rarest pediatric cardiomyopathy (**< 5%**) with the poorest prognosis (**50%** mortality at **2 years**), characterized by marked biatrial enlargement and normal ventricular dimensions, mandating early consideration of heart transplantation. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

left.title: Restrictive Cardiomyopathy (RCM)
points: Severe diastolic stiffness with normal ventricular wall thickness
Massive biatrial enlargement with normal or small ventricular cavities
Rapid progression of pulmonary vascular disease; early transplant listing needed

right.title: Constrictive Pericarditis
points: Rigid, calcified pericardium restricting end-diastolic filling
Prominent respiratory ventricular interdependence on Doppler echocardiography

steps.say: Failure of myocardial compaction during embryogenesis leads to a sponge-like ventricular wall with prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses.
steps.tx: Diagnostic criteria confirm **left ventricular non-compaction**. LVNC is characterized by prominent myocardial trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses, with non-compacted to compacted ratio **> 2.0:1** in end-systole (**Jenni criteria**) on echocardiography, causing heart failure and thromboembolic risk. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

nodes.label: Intrauterine arrest of physiological endomyocardial compaction during gestation
Formation of extensive deep intertrabecular recesses communicating with cavity
Development of two-layered myocardium with thin compacted outer epicardial layer
Jenni echocardiographic criteria: non-compacted to compacted ratio >2.0:1 in end-systole

steps.say: Comprehensive neurohormonal antagonism forms the medical foundation to arrest remodeling and improve survival in pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy.
steps.tx: Standard management applies **heart failure guideline therapy**. First-line neurohormonal blockade in pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy combines ACE inhibitors (**enalapril**), beta-blockers (**carvedilol**), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (**spironolactone**) to slow progressive remodeling and reduce mortality. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

rows: Reduces afterload and inhibits angiotensin-mediated myocardial fibrosis
Non-selective beta and alpha-1 blockade, anti-apoptotic, improves LVEF
Blocks aldosterone-induced cardiac collagen synthesis and retains potassium
